title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching scheduler has shown tail latency regressions for heterogeneous request mixes (short low-token requests coexisting with long context uses). This PR adjusts queueing semantics and fairness heuristics to prevent starvation of small requests while preserving batch efficiency. It also adds timeouts at multiple queueing stages to limit worst-case queueing latency under heavy load.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce per-priority queueing windows and a configurable fairness_weight that biases scheduler selection toward starving queues.
- Add starvation detector (moving-window request age histogram) and emergency drain policy that promotes starved queues into immediate scheduling.
- Enforce max_queueing_time_ms and per-request enqueue timestamps; requests exceeding the soft timeout are prioritized, requests exceeding hard timeout are rejected with a clear error code for higher-level routing.
- Improve scheduler backoff/jitter and time-bucketed metrics to make fairness decisions robust in noisy arrival patterns.
- Kernel-level noop: add trace points for scheduling decisions (no execution path change) to aid post-deploy analysis.
- Tests: unit tests for queue promotion, integration tests for mixed workload fairness, and new perf bench harness measuring p99 queueing latency with mixed workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1423)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks (local and CI)
- [x] Feature flags for rollout
- [x] Metrics and tracing added

Reasoning/details: The previous scheduler allowed long requests to accumulate large KV cache/sequence lengths and consume batching windows, which starved short, low-latency requests. We experimented with two approaches: strict priority lanes (caused throughput loss under certain mixes) and adaptive fairness (used here). Adaptive fairness uses a measured starvation score per queue: starvation_score = age_weight * avg_age_ms + backlog_weight * queue_length. The scheduler uses a tunable fairness_weight to adjust how much the starvation score overrides throughput-optimal batching. We also implemented a soft max_queueing_time_ms (default 120ms) to promote queued requests after that time, and a hard_queue_timeout_ms (default 2000ms) that triggers an explicit error path so caller can fallback to a lower-latency model.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag continuous_batcher.experimental_fair_scheduling, staged rollout to dedicated pools, perf canary on 5% of requests for 48h, monitor p50/p90/p99 queueing latency and throughput delta.

Notes: See comments below for specific reviewer suggestions and adjustments made in subsequent commits.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Overall looks good; two concerns: (1) ensure hard timeouts surface a distinct error code so the API layer can route to fallback, (2) add a short-circuit that avoids KV cache evictions when promoting short requests.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both in commit d4e5f6a; hard timeout now returns ERR_QUEUE_HARD_TIMEOUT and scheduler promotion avoids evicting active KV cache entries for promoted short requests.
Priya Natarajan: Please add telemetry for both promotion events and hard-timeout rejections (counts + histograms). Also, verify no perf regression on 8xA100 across our benchmark harness.

Maya Chen (author): Added time-bucketed counters and histograms in f0e1d2c. Perf harness results attached in CI. Minor regression observed at p50 (-2% throughput) in a synthetic long-only workload; it's expected and documented in release notes as tradeoff for p99 latency improvements on mixed workloads.
Elliot Park: suggest default fairness_weight=0.6 and lowering soft timeout to 100ms for hosted tier (to favor latency). We should gate defaults by deployment profile.
Maya Chen (author): Added deployment_profile overrides in runtime/continuous_batcher/config.h and defaults in infra/feature_flags/flags.yaml.
ci_checks: perf-ci (bench mixed-workload): pass (p99 queueing latency reduced by ~45% on test mix; p50 throughput -2% on long-only)
